name: Age range signal
plain: Asks the OS whether the user is in an age band, without giving a birth date.
meaning: Added to meet child safety laws. Both OSes return a range and a basis, not a date of birth.

android.note: Returns verified or supervised status and age lower and upper bounds

ios.note: Parent can approve sharing; returns bands such as 13 to 15

limits.headline: Can learn your age band, such as 13 to 15, but not your birth date
limits.user_action: You approve sharing your age range, or a parent approves for a child
can: Ask the phone for your age band (for example under 13, 13 to 15, or 18 and over)
Learn whether a parent supervises the account
Turn on age fitting features, like limited chat for teens
cannot: See your birth date or exact age
See your name, ID or address
Get an answer if you or a parent decline sharing (iPhone)
Verify your age with an ID check by itself
limits.reach_label: An age band, not a birth date
limits.differs: iPhone asks you and lets a parent approve. Android gives a verified or supervised status plus lower and upper age limits.

story.what_it_is: An app asks the phone which age group you are in, without learning your birth date.

marketing.name: Declared Age Range
marketing.pitch: Apps can ask for an age range that a parent or user has shared, without learning exact birth dates.

marketing.name: Play Age Signals
marketing.pitch: Google gives apps an age signal to help them follow child safety laws.

story.for_you: You or a parent set your age once. An app may ask for your age group, and you may see a prompt asking whether to share it. Teens may see a more limited version of the app.
story.for_makers: New laws push app makers to protect children, and a trustworthy age signal is easier than checking IDs. The rule is that the app gets a band like 13 to 15, not a date. Getting it wrong either shuts out young users or puts them in unsafe spaces.

use_cases.example: A social app switches off direct messages from strangers for people in the teen band.
A game turns off open voice chat and loot box offers for under 13 players.
A video app picks a kids profile when the age signal says a child is watching.
A dating app keeps minors out by asking the phone for an age check instead of a typed birthday.
A store hides age restricted items from younger shoppers.
A learning app asks a parent to approve a child's account when the age band says under 13.

risks: Age band can still be shared widely
story.android_note: Android apps get an age signal through Google Play for supervised accounts and in places where laws require it.
story.ios_note: iPhone shows a prompt and the person or a parent decides whether to share a range with the app.

technical_bounds: Range only, not exact birth date
Law status in Texas was in court at time of writing
